name: Shiva
kicker: Hindu god of destruction and change · One of the Trimurti
dates: Worshipped for thousands of years; one of Hinduism’s oldest deities
briefing: Shiva is one of Hinduism’s most important gods, worshipped by Hindus around the world as part of the Trimurti alongside Brahma the creator and Vishnu the preserver. Artists show him with a third eye, a crescent moon in his hair, and a trident called the trishula, often dancing as Nataraja, the “Lord of the Dance.” His devotees mark their foreheads with ash in his honor and tell stories of how his throat turned blue after he swallowed a poison that threatened to destroy the world.
answerHtml: Shiva (accept Siva or Mahadeva; prompt on “Nataraja” before it is read)

qb.tip: All 11 real tossups use the Trimurti (with Brahma and Vishnu) as the giveaway, and most also use Parvati, Ganesha’s elephant head, and the blue throat — those are must-know clues.

sample.note: the 11 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: The serpent Vasuki [“VAH-soo-kee”] coils around this deity’s neck, and he is said to have trapped the demon king Ravana under Mount Kailash after Ravana tried to lift the mountain. Followers mark their foreheads with three lines of ash and bring offerings to an aniconic pillar called a lingam in his honor.
tossups.r: This god once swallowed the Halahala poison that rose from the churning of the cosmic ocean. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction and change, husband of Parvati, who forms the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: This god is often shown wearing a tiger skin and holding a small hand-drum called a damaru. He also wears a necklace of skulls, a reminder that all things eventually come to an end.
tossups.r: This god’s dancing form is called Nataraja, “Lord of the Dance.” For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, the father of Ganesha and husband of Parvati.

tossups.p: This god burned the love god Kama to ash for interrupting his meditation. He later fathered the war god Kartikeya partly to help the other gods defeat the demon Taraka.
tossups.r: This god has a third eye on his forehead that can reduce things to ashes. For 10 points, name this Hindu deity who forms the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu, often shown with a blue throat.

tossups.p: In one story, this deity’s elephant-headed son won a race around his parents by arguing that they represented the whole world, beating his brother to a magic mango. In another story, this deity did not recognize that same son and removed his head, later reviving him with the head of an elephant.
tossups.r: That revived son is Ganesha. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, husband of Parvati, who forms the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: In the _Mahabharata_, this god gives the powerful Pashupatastra weapon to the warrior Arjuna. He is sometimes called Tripurantaka [“trih-poor-AHN-tuh-kuh”], “destroyer of three cities,” for defeating three demon fortresses with a single arrow.
tossups.r: This god is often shown with a third eye and a crescent moon in his hair. For 10 points, name this Hindu destroyer god, father of Ganesha and husband of Parvati.

tossups.p: Sacred temples dedicated to this god include Trimbakeshwar [“trim-buk-ESH-wur”] and Ramanathaswamy [“rah-muh-NAHT-uh-swah-mee”], and the number five is considered sacred to him. This god’s first father-in-law, Daksha, once left him out of an invitation to a sacrifice.
tossups.r: This god’s second wife is Parvati. For 10 points, name this member of the Hindu Trimurti along with Brahma and Vishnu, often shown dancing as Nataraja.

tossups.p: This god is said to have caught the Ganges River in his hair to break its fall from the heavens to Earth. He is usually shown with long, matted hair and a crescent moon resting on his head.
tossups.r: This god’s throat is permanently blue from swallowing a poison that threatened to destroy the universe. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction and transformation, husband of Parvati.

tossups.p: This god carries a three-pronged trident called a trishula [“trih-SHOO-lah”] and rides a white bull named Nandi. He is often shown with a third eye on his forehead.
tossups.r: This god’s wife is Parvati, and his sons are Ganesha and Kartikeya. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, who forms the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: After the gods and demons churned the cosmic ocean, this god swallowed the deadly Halahala poison that rose from it, which permanently turned his throat blue. He also has a third eye on his forehead that can burn things to ash.
tossups.r: This god is the father of the elephant-headed Ganesha. For 10 points, name this Hindu destroyer god, husband of Parvati, who completes the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: According to one story, this god did not recognize his own son and cut off his head, later reviving him with an elephant’s head. This same god is said to have trapped the demon king Ravana under Mount Kailash, where the serpent Vasuki coils around his neck.
tossups.r: That revived son is Ganesha. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, husband of Parvati, part of the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: Worshippers of this god mark their foreheads with three lines of ash and make offerings to a pillar-shaped symbol called a lingam. This god once burned the love god Kama to ashes for disturbing his meditation.
tossups.r: This god dances as Nataraja, “Lord of the Dance.” For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, father of Ganesha and husband of Parvati.

tossups.p: This god wears a necklace of skulls and, in the _Mahabharata_, gives the powerful Pashupatastra weapon to the hero Arjuna. He also carries a trident called a trishula.
tossups.r: This god’s throat is blue from swallowing a dangerous poison. For 10 points, name this Hindu destroyer god, who forms the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: This god fathered the god Kartikeya partly to help defeat the demon Taraka. Temples honoring this god include Trimbakeshwar and Ramanathaswamy, and he is often linked with the sacred number five.
tossups.r: This god rides a white bull named Nandi. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, husband of Parvati, part of the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: This god is sometimes called Tripurantaka for destroying three demon cities with a single arrow. He is also said to have caught the Ganges River as it fell from the sky, cushioning its fall in his hair.
tossups.r: This god has a third eye and wears a crescent moon on his head. For 10 points, name this Hindu deity who forms the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

tossups.p: This god holds a small drum called a damaru while dancing on a dwarf who stands for ignorance, a form of him known as Nataraja. His throat turned permanently blue after he swallowed a poison that rose during the churning of the cosmic ocean.
tossups.r: This god’s wife is Parvati, and his sons are Ganesha and Kartikeya. For 10 points, name this Hindu god of destruction, who completes the Trimurti with Brahma and Vishnu.

trap.title: Which third of the Trimurti?
trap.body: Clues about the Trimurti fit three different gods: Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver, and Shiva the destroyer. A clue about four heads or a swan means Brahma, and one about a conch shell or ten avatars means Vishnu, so do not buzz on “Trimurti” alone.
trap.fix: Listen for Shiva’s own symbols: the trident (trishula), the third eye, the crescent moon, the blue throat, or his dancing Nataraja form. Those belong to Shiva alone.
